title: A Letter After Midnight
excerpt: Every night a letter appears beneath her door, written by someone who knows her too well.

sections.title: The First Letter
paragraphs: The first letter arrived without a stamp, folded twice beneath the apartment door.
It contained one sentence: You still hum when you're nervous.
Only one person had ever noticed that, and he had been gone for six years.

sections.title: The Familiar Hand
paragraphs: The handwriting changed each night, as if someone were trying too hard to disguise it.
But memory is stubborn. She recognized the hesitation before every capital R.
On the seventh night she waited beside the door instead of sleeping.

sections.title: Morning
paragraphs: She opened the door before the paper touched the floor.
Some stories begin with introductions. Theirs began again with a silence neither of them knew how to survive.
